title: Cache invariant multilevel triangular pivots
evidence: Tower2304 active nodes/137 iterations and dense1584/34 spend most of their109/32ms cold step in the cooperative solver. Each multilevel smoother repeatedly performs12 FP64 divisions per node by six unchanged Cholesky pivots. N06a showed that sacrificing parallelism is harmful; this preserves its decomposition.
proposed_mechanism: Produce six guarded reciprocal pivots alongside existing factor construction, retaining the21 original factors. Thread-local V-cycle triangular solves multiply cached normal reciprocals; exceptional reciprocal ranges retain division. Native inverse recovery keeps a null cache and original arithmetic. No extra kernel, CPU count readback or convergence relaxation.
affected_scenarios: all city stages as small-component/setup controls
estimated_application_ms_saved: 0 to20ms tower,0 to5ms dense, near zero city; low-confidence upper bounds, not predictions. Extra48bytes/node and factor setup can regress.
confidence: Medium reuse/lifetime correctness, low-to-medium performance; changed rounding must pass original equilibrium/force gates.
experiment_cost: Five private headers, matched isolated runtime/oracle builds; existing hierarchy/large-cycle/current-load tests and normal memory checks, targeted20/20/20 plus light before full acceptance.
supporting_measurements: Lower whole-step tower/dense time with unchanged physical quality/convergence caps; reduced repeated divide work without spills/setup or city regressions.
refuting_measurements: Memory/lifetime failure, altered physical verdict, no application improvement, register pressure or extra cache traffic exceeds divide savings.
scope: Independent compatible baseline, no N14 closure/N15/N16/N19/N20 composition. Different from lower-priority N11 free-nullspace projection reciprocals. No completed-experiment credit until measured.
